results.summary_before: This project implements a compact 4-bit microcoded CPU that fetches and executes instructions from an external SPI RAM, such as a 23LC512 chip or an RP2040 emulating it. The CPU uses the SPI Pmod interface for program storage and provides 8-bit output and a CPU_VALID signal. It is designed for the TinyTapeout GF180MCU platform and verified using cocotb with Icarus Verilog. The design requires external SPI RAM hardware for operation.
results.summary: This project implements a compact 4-bit microcoded CPU that fetches and executes instructions from an external SPI RAM, such as a 23LC512 chip or an RP2040 emulating it. The CPU uses the SPI Pmod interface for program storage and provides an 8-bit output register plus a CPU_VALID signal. It is designed for the TinyTapeout GF180MCU platform and verified using cocotb with Icarus Verilog. The design requires external SPI RAM hardware for operation.

results.summary_before: This design allows a user to tap a button twice to set a beat tempo, which then causes the eight outputs to chase in a barrel-shift pattern at that rate. When the mode pin is not asserted, the first output emits digital noise generated by an LFSR. It requires external hardware: a button for tapping, a switch for mode selection, LEDs on the outputs, and an audio amplifier for the noise output. Notable for its simple interactive beat detection and noise generation, implemented in Amaranth.

results.summary_before: This design plays multiple tunes on a piezo speaker connected across two output pins using differential PWM modulation. It converts RTTL ringtone data into Verilog and allows tune selection via input pins. A 10 kHz clock and a reset pulse are required to start playback. The project is notable for its use of differential PWM to drive a piezo speaker directly.

results.summary_before: This is a simple 4-bit CPU with a 4-bit accumulator, a 7-bit program counter, two 7-bit index registers, and a carry bit. It has 25 instructions and is designed to run with external SRAM and a 7-bit address latch, with code loaded externally. The CPU includes an on-chip SRAM block for data access and a 4-deep hardware call stack. Testing requires a 7-bit external address latch and SRAM.

results.summary_before: This is an 8-bit version of the MoonBase 4-bit CPU, featuring an 8-bit accumulator, a 12-bit program counter, two 13-bit index registers, and a carry bit. It has 33 instructions and is designed to run with external SRAM and a 12-bit address latch, with code loaded externally. The CPU includes an on-chip SRAM block for data access and a 3-deep hardware call stack. An assembler is available online, and testing requires a 7-bit external address latch and SRAM.

results.summary_before: This is a pseudo-random number generator based on a 16-bit Fibonacci linear-feedback shift register. It produces one new random bit per clock cycle, with the last 8 bits available on the output pins, and supports loading a custom seed value via the data_in pin when load_en is high. The design is implemented in Wokwi and can be tested by manually clocking the circuit and observing the output on a hex display. No external hardware is needed.
